stories.headline: Cyclone Akwan begins landfall along India's east coast with strong winds and heavy rain
stories.title: Cyclone Akwan begins landfall along India's east coast with strong winds and heavy rain
stories.summary: Cyclone Akwan begins landfall along India's east coast with strong winds and heavy rain
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the cyclonic storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts early on Friday, says the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

“Latest satellite imagery indicates the land interaction commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with the Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ entered into the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts,” informed IMD on Friday (November 20, 2026).

“The severe cyclonic storm Akvan over the westcentral Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards with the speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours, weakened into a cyclonic storm and lay centred over the same region about 110 km southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 170 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha) and 250 km south-southwest of Puri (Odisha),” informed the IMD bulletin.

“It is likely to continue to move north-northwestward and cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by the forenoon of November 20, 2026, with the maximum sustained wind speed of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph,” it further said.
Director of Bhubaneswar Meteorological Centre Manorama Mohanty said the duration of the landfall process would be a long process which could stretch over seven to eight hours.
Meanwhile, coastal Odisha districts have started receiving heavy rain under the influence of the cyclone.
